text: Driftwood's biggest sale of the year opens at 9 AM. Traffic climbs sharply in the first twenty minutes, then surges to nine or ten times baseline, triggering a series of rapid HPA scale-events that take checkout-api from 6 replicas to nearly 30 within forty minutes — exactly the bursty pattern last lesson's load test never reproduced.

By 9:45, the FinOps dashboard tells a reassuring story: cluster-wide CPU averaging 58 percent with headroom to spare, cost burn-down tracking the forecasted line, and storefront's cost share scaling proportionally with traffic. Theo reports to Casey Lindqvist: on budget, scaling as planned, nothing to flag.

At 10:15, a handful of scattered customer-support reports land in platform-oncall — a few mentions of slow checkouts, nothing resembling a flood. Theo checks the FinOps dashboard again: still 58 percent, still on budget. Nothing on the one screen built to judge platform health shows anything unusual.

This lesson doesn't resolve that note, and that's deliberate. A few scattered complaints against a healthy-looking cost and capacity dashboard isn't a five-alarm signal on its own — it's a loose thread. What it's actually connected to is where this capstone goes next.
